Hi Neha,

We are working through the security questionnaire for our procurement team and have a few nonstandard asks around data deletion and keystore residency for the Private deployment. Two quick items we need confirmed before we can sign:

1) Keystore residency: does Redwood offer an onshore-only keystore residency option (keys stored in customer VPC / customer-managed KMS) and can you provide artifacts demonstrating key deletion/rotation events?

2) Automated erase & proof artifacts: our compliance requires an automated, auditable erase workflow that produces a tamper-evident proof-of-delete (manifest, hash chain or signed certificate) for tenant-bounded inference logs and derived telemetry. Can you confirm the API/endpoint, expected SLA for certificate issuance post-erase, and sample artifacts you would provide (SIG/CAIQ references preferred)?

We also have a potential legal hold scenario for a small subset of transactions — can you outline how Redwood would support a temporary retention hold and then produce a final delete certificate once lifted?

We are on a tight contracting window (aiming to finish by end of month). If possible, please share sample evidence artifacts and a short timeline for producing final CAIQ/SIG attachments.

Thanks,
Laura Stein
Head of InfoSec
Healix Labs

Hi Laura — thanks, quick few operational notes from the CS/ops side:

Planned deliverables for your SIG/CAIQ review:
- Redwood_keystore_handback_playbook.pdf (high-level: keystore residency options, handback steps, S3 export mechanics)
- erase_manifest_sample.csv (sample: tenant_id, object_type, object_id, delete_timestamp, sha256, signing_key_id)
- caiq_section_A7_attestation.pdf (text we place into CAIQ A.7 / Data Retention & Deletion section with our control statement)

SLA and process notes:
- Erase request submission -> erase completed (typical): 1–8 hours depending on object count and batch scheduling.
- Proof-of-delete certificate issued (signed artifact): standard commitment 48–72 hours after successful erase job completes. We can discuss a contract amendment if Healix needs 24 hours.
- For customer-managed keystores in customer VPC: Redwood will not retain plaintext key material. We can provide signed export manifests and a keystore-handback checklist.

Legal hold flow: we maintain a kept-record flag per-tenant. If a hold is requested, we pin relevant objects and provide a forensics manifest showing scope. Once the hold is released, the erase API can be triggered and the proof-of-delete artifact generated on release.

I've attached the three artifacts above for your review; Irene, please confirm the API endpoint and sample payload we should share with Healix security.

Thanks — happy to jump on the call tomorrow at 10:00am PT if that works for you, Laura.

--- Forwarded message ---
On Thu, Apr 15, 2026 at 11:08 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> (attachments: redwood_keystore_handback_playbook.pdf, erase_manifest_sample.csv, caiq_section_A7_attestation.pdf)

Technical details (summary):
- Erase API endpoint (tenant-scoped, authenticated): POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/erase
- Sample JSON payload: {
  "objects": [ {"type": "inference_log", "id": "abc123"}, ... ],
  "requestor": "healix-admin@healixlabs.com",
  "request_reason": "contracted-data-disposition"
}
- On success the API returns a job_id; job status endpoint /erase/{job_id}/status provides progress and final delete manifest location.
- Proof artifact: signed JSON-LD manifest (or CSV) containing deleted object list, deletion timestamps, sha256 of deleted blobs, signing_key_id and signature block. We sign manifests using our operational signing key and can provide the public cert chain for verification.

Keystore-handback notes:
- For customer-managed KMS/HSM we provide a handback checklist that verifies no Redwood-held plaintext key material remains, and we provide signed logs of any key rotation/deletion events.
- For Redwood-managed keystores we can do an export into a customer-controlled storage location and then rotate/delete server-side copies; all events are recorded in the signed manifest.

One caveat: if a legal/regulatory hold is asserted by your legal team, we will mark the objects as retained and will not perform the erase until cleared via an authorized release request. We can record the hold issuance and release events with the same signed artifact model.

Irene Choi
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
